**sqlpipe Architecture Overview**

sqlpipe is a streaming pipeline that exports PostgreSQL data to S3 as Parquet files. The system comprises three concurrent stages connected by bounded channels.

The **Reader** opens a server-side cursor against Postgres and fetches rows in configurable batches (default 10,000 rows). It deserializes each batch into an in-memory Arrow record batch and pushes it downstream, applying backpressure when the channel fills.

The **Converter** receives Arrow batches and accumulates them into Parquet row groups. Once a row group reaches its target size, it flushes the encoded bytes to the upload stage. This design keeps memory bounded while producing well-sized row groups for query performance.

The **Uploader** initiates an S3 multipart upload and streams each row group as a part. It retries transient failures with exponential backoff and completes the upload after the final part, ensuring atomic object creation.
